accepted.label: Folding Back Procedure
accepted.description: The folding back procedure solves a decision tree from right to left: at chance nodes, compute EMV; at decision nodes, select the alternative with the highest EMV. The EMV at the root is the optimal EMV.
coverage_criteria: Apply the folding back procedure to a small decision tree to find the optimal decision and its EMV.
Explain the rule for selecting at a decision node during folding back.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate covers the overall folding back procedure. It is a standalone concept because it describes the full algorithm, which is distinct from the specific net benefit calculation.

accepted.label: Net Benefit Calculation at Decision Nodes
accepted.description: At a decision node, the cost of each option is subtracted from its expected outcome value to compute net benefit. The option with the highest net benefit is selected.
coverage_criteria: Given a decision node with costs and outcome values, compute net benefits for each option.
Identify the optimal choice based on the highest net benefit.
accepted.merge_rationale: This candidate details the subtraction of costs from expected outcomes to compute net benefit, which is a finer-grained step within the folding back procedure. It represents a distinct concept at a more detailed level, so it stands alone.
